mbm-2276.clue: I can fold it with my eyes closed now.
mbm-2276.quote: I spent my first whole karate class trying to tie my belt. My teacher let me practice on a chair. Twenty years later that same chair wears the belts of all my new students.

mbm-2277.clue: Nobody wanted the last slice of pizza till the board came out.
mbm-2277.quote: We made a game of delivering wooden pizzas across a crooked cardboard city. My aunt parked her piece by the bakery and opened her own restaurant. We had to write a new rule.

mbm-2278.clue: My biggest laugh came from inside a chimney.
mbm-2278.quote: I was the stagehand who had to lower snow through a cardboard chimney. My mitten fell through instead. The actor caught it, put it on, and got applause. I sent the other one down on closing night.

mbm-2279.clue: I take a folding ruler on our dates.
mbm-2279.quote: My partner kept losing the ball inside the plaster whale at mini golf. I brought a ruler to fish it out. Turns out the whale had swallowed twelve balls and a pink hair clip.

mbm-2280.clue: My wristwatch has a round pale twin.
mbm-2280.quote: I lay in the sun with my watch off for once. My sister made a paper dial for the pale circle on my wrist. Apparently it’s always lunchtime there.

mbm-2281.clue: I used to think breakfast was over when the tide came in.
mbm-2281.quote: We use an empty cereal box for the wickets on the beach. A wave flattened it last Sunday. My dad unfolded the box, laid it on the sand and declared we were playing for a new breakfast record.

mbm-2282.clue: My dragon takes its bow the hard way.
mbm-2282.quote: I gave my marionette a jaw that opens separately. At rehearsal its little wooden teeth caught my sleeve. I bowed and the dragon bowed too. We’ve kept that ending ever since.

mbm-2283.clue: There’s a tiny moon in my shoe.
mbm-2283.quote: My glow-in-the-dark ball got wedged in the last hole at mini golf. I fished it out and stuck it in my sneaker for the ride home. Dad nearly jumped out of his skin when my foot lit up.

mbm-2284.clue: I can tell time with my knees.
mbm-2284.quote: My favorite sun lounger sits where a striped umbrella makes moving shadows. I read until the last stripe reaches my knee. Then I trade places with my sister so her corner warms up too.

mbm-2285.clue: I lost on purpose to a mountain of cherries.
mbm-2285.quote: In the cherry pie contest I bit into a perfect five-pointed crust star. I saved the star and finished one bite behind. My little daughter wore it on her paper crown all afternoon.

mbm-2286.clue: I keep a towel tied to the same post.
mbm-2286.quote: I spent all summer trying to drop one water ski and keep going. The morning I finally managed it nobody saw but a gull. It stayed on the post like a judge waiting for the next run.

mbm-2287.clue: Our butler lives next to the peppercorns.
mbm-2287.quote: I read aloud to my family on Sundays. My sister handles footsteps by rattling a jar of peppercorns. I snap a bay leaf stem whenever the butler knocks. We gave him three extra entrances last week because my grandpa kept asking to let him in.

mbm-2288.clue: I make the scorecards fit in a matchbox.
mbm-2288.quote: I draw the silliest obstacle on each mini-golf scorecard before I fold it. Twelve years of family vacations fit in one old matchbox. The giant chicken course gets the top bunk.

mbm-2289.clue: I paddle better with my mouth full.
mbm-2289.quote: My cousin says I call every stroke too early. She handed me a caramel and we paddled a whole mile in perfect time. She brings a paper bag of them for rough water now.

mbm-2290.clue: I let the little artist keep the title page.
mbm-2290.quote: A sparrow walked across my wet field sketch and left a perfect set of tracks. I drew its portrait around the prints. It's the first page I show anyone who asks about birding.

mbm-2291.clue: My tent pegs wear bright little socks.
mbm-2291.quote: I tripped over our tent ropes twice in the same evening. My cousin slipped her spare striped socks over the pegs. We had the funniest-looking tent on the hill and made it through breakfast upright.

mbm-2292.quote: My brother gave me his old referee’s shirt for our quilt. I saved its little chest pocket for the whistle. Family arguments under that blanket have a pretty efficient halftime.

mbm-2293.clue: I’m the keeper of the pause button.
mbm-2293.quote: Our anime club freezes one frame each week and everybody draws it from memory. My robot penguin looked more like a kettle. The others made it our mascot, handle and all.

mbm-2294.clue: Our smallest mechanic runs a delivery service.
mbm-2294.quote: My model robot kept dropping the spare screws in its arms. I built it a little red cart and put the whole repair shop on wheels. It delivers parts from one end of my workbench to the other.

mbm-2295.clue: I carry a spoon for the view.
mbm-2295.quote: My gran used to tap the summit marker with a teaspoon to let the mountain know she'd arrived. I hiked up with her bent spoon in my pocket. It still makes the tiniest ping.

mbm-2296.clue: My oldest square used to miss the school bus.
mbm-2296.quote: I cut a red square from the lunch bag I carried in first grade. There’s still a faint rectangle where my name tag sat. I stitched it in the middle so Mum could find it from across the room.

mbm-2297.clue: The green stripe is there because the shutters stuck.
mbm-2297.quote: I was painting the barber shop when the owner wrestled one shutter open halfway. I liked that crooked green stripe so much I made him leave it till sundown. He came out to check my work after every haircut.

mbm-2298.clue: I always try the pockets first.
mbm-2298.quote: My flea-market raincoat had a tiny toy horse in its pocket. I went back the next Saturday and found the seller's kid. We swapped the horse for a striped marble. Best bargain I ever made.

mbm-2299.clue: My lift pass is attached to a teaspoon.
mbm-2299.quote: I broke the zip pull on my ski jacket before the first run. The lodge cook loaned me a teaspoon and a bit of string. It chimed on every turn. She recognized me before I got to the counter.
